title: Le probleme 3n+1 : y a-t-il des cycles non triviaux ? (III)
notes: Images des Mathematiques, CNRS, 2011; the third part of an expository series by the author of eliahou-1993-collatz-cycle-lengths. NOT READ -- images.math.cnrs.fr, its page-freeze mirror, idm-old.math.cnrs.fr and lmpa.univ-littoral.fr are all refused by this environment's egress policy. Found 20 September 2026 as a link on OEIS A020857 (decimal expansion of log_2 3), which the laboratory reached while reading the comment fields of the sequences around Paper B's survivor recursion. WHY IT IS REGISTERED. The laboratory reproduces Eliahou's 1993 lattice exactly at floor 2^40 -- 301994a + 17087915b + 85137581c with b >= 1, least period 17087915 -- so a later statement of the same bound by the same author is directly comparable machinery, not background. AN UNATTRIBUTED NUMBER, RECORDED AS SUCH. A figure 17026679261 circulates as a lower bound on nontrivial 3n+1 cycle length and appears independently in several places (T. Ian Martiny, 'New Lower Bound on Cycle Length for the 3n+1 Problem', Univ. of Pittsburgh; M. Twarog's 2020 notes; Lagarias's Annotated Bibliography II), so the number is real rather than a search artefact. A search summary attributed it to THIS article; that attribution is NOT established, Martiny's title suggests the bound may be his, and nothing here was read at source. The number is therefore recorded as circulating and unattributed, and is NOT entered into any laboratory table. Settling it needs the article, or Martiny's paper, read directly. Do not cite for anything until read.
